source.note: The copy+ETB-UNTAP infinite -- the untap-arm SIBLING of kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel (which closes via BLINK). Kiki-Jiki's '{T}: Create a token that's a copy of target nonlegendary creature you control, except it has haste' copies Zealous Conscripts; GraftCopyInheritance (PortGraphEngine.cs, copy-inheritance-scope.md Decision 2/3) grafts the copy's inherited abilities onto the token. The copy (a Zealous Conscripts, which natively has Haste and is also given haste by Kiki) enters -> its ETB fires and untaps KIKI ITSELF -> Kiki, untapped IN PLACE, re-taps to copy again. VERIFIED Zealous Conscripts oracle text (oracle-cards.json): 'Haste\nWhen this creature enters, gain control of target permanent until end of turn. Untap that permanent. It gains haste until end of turn.' The closing resource is Kiki's {T} tap cost; it is renewed by the ETB's mandatory 'Untap that permanent', NOT by a blink -- Kiki is never exiled/returned, it stays the SAME object and is merely untapped, so (unlike Kiki x Restoration Angel) there is NO summoning-sickness question at all and Kiki's own haste is NOT load-bearing here. No mana is spent in the cycle, so there is NO CR-808/section-8 mana floor. TIER: still AMBER, but on a SINGLE floor rather than Restoration Angel's two. The untap is MANDATORY (no 'you may' -- contrast Restoration Angel's Gated optional blink, which BlinkReachesSource floors via Trilean.Unknown), so the OPTIONALITY floor is GONE. What remains is the object-identity Overlap: 'gain control of TARGET permanent ... untap that permanent' is a chosen target, and the operator cannot certify the target IS Kiki rather than some other permanent (guard:self-watch, CR 603.6e/400.7) -> Overlaps, never Subsumes -> AMBER. This corroborates that the object-identity Overlap ALONE caps the copy-untap closing hop to AMBER, independent of optionality. CORROBORATES Kiki's copy arm at a 2nd combo: K1 (emit:copy, stem=copy, attrs {}) and K2 (consume tap:self) are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel witnesses (same faithful live projection: Kiki dump = emit:copy + tap:self). PARSE GAP (reported, not authored around): the live dump projects Zealous Conscripts as emit:gaincontrol + emit:keywordability(haste) + etb:creature:self (stem=deployment:creature, isSelf=true, GREEN) -- the 'Untap that permanent' clause does NOT project a separate emit:untap:permanent; it is currently ABSORBED into the coarse emit:gaincontrol (the compound 'gain control ... untap ...' clause). So ZC1 (the ETB self-watch) is FAITHFULLY parsed, but ZC2 (the structure:untap emit) is the PARSER TARGET, exactly like the Deadeye gold is the parser target for deployment[manner=blink]. The closing bridge is authored in honest ADR-3 vocabulary against that target; the gold witnesses faithfully once the parser slices the untap clause out of the gaincontrol compound. No edhrec/popularity figure available in the testbed source -- popularity omitted (not fabricated).

judge.ref: interaction-judge PASS (accretion batch 9, 2026-07-17): 9/9 PASS, no false GREEN. GREEN-on-new-rule golds (Teysa policy:trigger-multiplier, Heliod policy:counter-supplies-cost) CR-sound; untap-renews-tap collapse ruled SOUND (one relation, GREEN ceiling, guard-floored edges); pili-pala untap-to-mana split ruled SOUND-DISTINCT (external-tapper vs intrinsic self-tap inference).

Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker.note: THE COPY ARM -- '{T}: Create a token that's a copy of target nonlegendary creature you control, except it has haste.' Permanent token-copy (CR 707.2). BYTE-IDENTICAL to kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel K1 (live engine emit:copy, family=copy, stem=copy, manner=null, isSelf=false; the permanent variant carries no in-axis facets, so attrs is empty). CORROBORATES Kiki's copy arm at a 2nd, structurally distinct combo (the close here is ETB-UNTAP, not blink). GraftCopyInheritance resolves this copy's target filter against Zealous Conscripts and clones its ports under a synthesized copy identity.

the {T} activation cost of K1 (dump: consume tap:self). BYTE-IDENTICAL to kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel K2. THE loop-closing resource: renewed when the copy's ETB untaps Kiki (E3). Contrast Kiki x Restoration Angel, where the renewal is a BLINK (Kiki re-enters as a NEW untapped object); here Kiki is untapped IN PLACE (same object, no re-entry, no summoning sickness).

Zealous Conscripts.note: the copy's inherited ETB self-watch -- 'When this creature enters ...' (FAITHFULLY PARSED: live dump consume etb:creature:self, stem=deployment:creature, isSelf=true, GREEN). In the loop this fires on the COPY's own entry (grafted onto the token Kiki just created). Same self-watch shape as Restoration Angel R1 / emiel MU0 / deadeye PD1.

THE UNTAP ARM -- 'Untap that permanent' (the second sentence of the ETB, acting on the 'target permanent' from the first). MANDATORY: no 'you may' -> no optionality floor (contrast Restoration Angel R2's Gated 'you may' blink). target=chosen + qty=1 captures 'that [target] permanent' -- a single chosen target the operator cannot prove IS Kiki (object-identity Overlap -> guard:self-watch). PARSER TARGET / PARSE GAP: the live dump does NOT project this port -- Zealous Conscripts currently projects emit:gaincontrol (the compound 'gain control of target permanent ... untap that permanent' clause) + emit:keywordability + etb:creature:self; the untap is absorbed into the coarse gaincontrol emit and not sliced out as structure:untap. Authored as the faithful ADR-3 target (as the Deadeye gold authors deployment[manner=blink] before blink parses). NOTE structure:untap gains a `target` attr witness here (deadeye PD2 used subtype/control/qty on 'up to five lands'; `target` is licensed_by ['*'] so the accretion is licit) -- surfaced, not silent.

notes: the {T} tap cost (K2) drives the copy emit (K1) -- a card-internal cost->effect wiring (byte-identical to kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel E0; cf. displacer DK1->DK2, conviction CV1->CV2)

THE GRAFT edge. CR 707.2: the copier definitely creates the copy token; the copy (a Zealous Conscripts) enters the battlefield -> its inherited ETB (ZC1) fires (CR 603.6, an ETB trigger is not optional to FIRE). Engine GraftCopyInheritance synthesizes exactly this as a card-defined GREEN edge copy-emit -> copy-etb-consume (PortGraphEngine.cs ~281-285). Same graft as kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel E1.

the copy's ETB effect IS the untap -- a card-internal trigger->effect wiring (cf. Restoration Angel R1->R2 the blink; emiel MU0->MU1). Inherited on the copy via the graft. The 'Untap that permanent' clause is the ETB's payload.

THE CLOSING HOP. The copy's ETB untaps Kiki IN PLACE -> the {T} tap cost K2 is renewed (Kiki is the SAME object, not blinked -- CR 400.7 identity unchanged, no re-entry). AMBER on a SINGLE floor: object-identity Overlap -- 'gain control of target permanent ... untap that permanent' is a chosen target and the operator cannot prove the untap lands on Kiki specifically rather than some other permanent (guard:self-watch, CR 603.6e/400.7). Contrast kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel E3, which is AMBER on TWO floors (the Gated 'you may' optional blink PLUS object identity): here the untap is MANDATORY, so the optionality floor is absent -- this witnesses that the object-identity Overlap ALONE caps the copy-close to AMBER. Distinct from bridge:blink-renews-tap (Kiki re-enters as a NEW object) and bridge:untap-land-to-mana (renews MANA, not a tap-ability cost) -> new rule bridge:untap-renews-tap.

guards.desc: corroborates the self-watch object-identity guard on the ETB-untap closing hop: a chosen-target untap ('untap that [target] permanent') whose target only Overlaps -- never provably Subsumes -- the specific tap-gated copier (Kiki) cannot certify the untap lands on Kiki rather than another permanent (object identity the operator can't see) -> floors AMBER. A NEW witness type for the guard: it caps AMBER here EVEN THOUGH the effect is mandatory (no optionality), isolating the object-identity floor from the optionality floor that co-caps the blink dual (kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel).

bridges.desc: an untap (structure:untap emit) renews a tap-based cost/ability (tap consume): the untapped permanent's {T} activated ability or tap-cost becomes available again (CR 701.26 untap keyword action; CR 107.5 the {T} cost; CR 602 re-activation). Ceiling GREEN -- a mandatory, universal untap reliably renews the tap (witnessed by Intruder Alarm's 'untap all creatures'); individual edges floor to AMBER via their own residual guards: object-identity Overlap on a targeted untap (guard:self-watch) or a cumulative counter co-cost (guard:untap-cost-accrues-counter). Collapses the batch-9 per-outlet siblings (ETB-targeted / universal-creature / self-via-counter) into one relation -- the differences are the untap's trigger/target (far side of the emit), not the untap->tap bridge.

assertions.because: the graft: CR 707.2 the copier definitely creates the copy and CR 603.6 its ETB fires on entry (card-defined GREEN, matching engine GraftCopyInheritance)

the closing hop rests SOLELY on the object-identity Overlap (guard:self-watch) -- the mandatory untap targets a chosen permanent the operator cannot prove is Kiki; there is NO optionality floor (contrast Restoration Angel's Gated blink)

the untap is MANDATORY (no 'you may') and untaps Kiki IN PLACE (same object, no re-entry, no summoning sickness, no mana), so the only irreducible floor is the chosen-target object-identity Overlap -- isolating the guard:self-watch floor from the optionality floor that co-caps the blink dual (kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel E3)

K1 (emit:copy, stem=copy, attrs {}) and K2 (consume tap:self) are byte-identical to the kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel witnesses -- Kiki's copy arm is now witnessed at a 2nd, structurally distinct combo (ETB-untap close vs blink close)

Zealous Conscripts currently projects emit:gaincontrol (absorbing the 'untap that permanent' clause) + emit:keywordability + etb:creature:self -- the structure:untap emit ZC2 is NOT yet AST-derivable; this gold is the parser target for slicing the untap out of the gaincontrol compound, mirroring how deadeye-x-peregrine-drake is the parser target for deployment[manner=blink]
